meta.title: Chakra Meditation · Flow Atlas
meta.scope: Current working-tree behavior. Sky and audio changes have static/unit evidence only; no device listening verification. Browser preview was declined. Branches are composed across maps; this is not a claim that every browser, timing race, or setting combination has been runtime-tested.

graphs.subtitle: Navigation, journey families, supporting systems, and exits.

Main mode selection, chakra choices, intention, duration and consultation.
Settings → isolated activity → return to Experiment screen. See Experiments map.
Shots → Music Only → Sleep → focused or standard guided start. See mode map.
Separate HTML pages. Consultation produces a review; repertory can prepare a custom Shot.
Shared timer, audio, narration, visuals, mixer, pause and stop.
JSON scripts, language bundles, Web Audio, Piper worker, localStorage and service worker.
Guided and Sleep flows update local stats; return to room or eligible Earn link.

Warm model; serial worker requests; synthesize first two sentences and keep one ahead.
Select matching voice and locale; apply pace/pitch/volume; speak each sentence.

graphs.title: Audio signal architecture
graphs.subtitle: Logical buses; shared filters are expanded in selected-node details.
rows: Decoded clips → voice gain → warmth and clarity filters; parallel Voice Space reverb.
SeamlessLoop → mantra gain/filter → dry path and reverb tail → spatial panner.
Chakra/sleep drones, elemental layers and transition/Shot tones use their respective generator routes.
Equal-power repeat overlaps → independent loop level → linear music entry gain; dry gate and Music Space send; music spatial panner.
MediaElementSource → dedicated Video gain → music spatial panner and Music Space send.
Local manifest or user URL → equal-power layered loops → blur and spatial depth/panner.

Low-cut → Eyes Close filter → voice-carve filter → exciter → presence → compressor through one path. Filtered duplicate and transition swell removed; dedicated reverb tails remain. Music peaking EQ applies -3 dB when ducked and 0 dB at full level. Voice Space is independent of Spatial Sound; Spatial Off ramps added pan modulation to zero.
Shared chain ends in limiter and AudioContext destination. Bell gain connects directly to limiter.
Separate speechSynthesis output; not processed by the shared Web Audio graph.
notes: Narration ducks music. Music/mantra gates overlap on entry and exit; completion does not restore music and uses one music exit envelope. Loop volume is separate from repeat crossfades; overlap is bounded to half the buffer, and source cleanup follows audio time through pause. Music entry is linear with no second long source fade. Intentional silence and explicit mute remain. Spatial choices: Off, Stereo, Headphones, Room. Browser/device output and audibility need listening verification; timer throttling and silence inside recordings are not ruled out.

graphs.title: Visuals and browser lifecycle
graphs.subtitle: Natural sky, chakra imagery, immersion and optional capabilities.
rows: Load NaturalNightSky before app; cache a seeded 700–2,400-star backdrop with faint procedural galactic luminance and dark dust lanes. Neutral night gradient replaces drifting colored CSS clouds.
Success updates observer and named celestial bodies; denied/unavailable retains approximate sky. Fine background stars are procedural, not a location-calibrated star catalog.
Reduced motion renders a static frame; changes to the OS preference immediately stop/restart animation. At most 110 stars shimmer; positions remain fixed.
Chakra color, aura, deity/symbol selection, progress dots and narration ticker.

Resize rebuilds the cached backdrop with deterministic placement; normal frames composite it and shimmer selected stars. Celestial positions refresh at most once per minute. Textured lunar illumination is phase-cached; planets are small points and the Moon is intentionally unlabeled. Named planets and bright stars use compact 11 px labels with 30% text plus 15% backing and outline. Backing alone receives a soft 3 px blur; text/outline stay sharp and underlying stars are not blurred. Unsupported canvas filters retain plain backing. Meteors occur singly after a delayed start, then every 45–120 seconds. Hidden pages cancel animation and clear meteors.

Natural/Aura/Holographic retain CSS effects. Sacred Depth uses a local WebGL 2.5D scene: authored smooth relief displacement, luminance-derived highlight lighting and textured atmosphere around source transparency. Original artwork alpha is preserved. A read-only mantra analyser gently modulates highlights with two-second smoothing; no microphone or audio gain change. Capped at 30 fps, 960 px longest drawing edge and 1.25 DPR. Pause freezes the renderer; hidden pages stop frames; reduced motion draws a static scene. Stop or Eyes Close restores the original image. WebGL/texture failure or context loss falls back to CSS; restored context can retry. Scene breathing is decorative, not synchronized to separate Box Breathing instructions.
Explicit user brightness, Sleep dimming and Eyes Close remain honored. Eyes Close suppresses decorative motion/light; audio comfort filtering remains unchanged.
Only responds to user/browser fullscreen; app-container fullscreen controls have pointer/focus reveal.
Best-effort request in supported routes; failure is swallowed; release on stop/completion.
notes: The lunar surface and background star field are illustrative procedural renderings; existing named-body location calculations remain approximate. New sky has no external assets or network dependency and caps DPR at 1.5. Static/unit checks cover bounded work, stable placement, reduced-motion draws and lunar illumination. Browser/device appearance remains unverified because the preview request was declined.

graphs.title: Persistence, caching and network
graphs.subtitle: Local state and the actual service-worker request routing.
rows: HTML/CSS/JS, JSON, audio/video and Piper assets.
Languages, voices, durations, chakra choices, intention, custom script, mixer settings and stats; consultation stores answers separately.
Experience modes, intimate unlock and mood ambience enablement reset on page load. No full in-progress journey restore.
cache.addAll shell/content/audio assets; one rejected required asset rejects precache installation. skipWaiting requested.
Claim clients; delete every cache except three exact current shell/Piper/language names.
Manifest and matching pleasure files use network no-store, despite manifest appearing in precache.
Cache-first, fetch on miss, cache successful response. Piper recognizes local assets and Hugging Face voice URLs.
Exact caches.match(request), otherwise network; ordinary misses are not added to cache.
Only matching cached requests can work offline. Timestamped content and versioned shell requests may miss unversioned precache entries.
notes: Video is not precached. Browsing tests disable service workers. Offline startup and upgrades are verification priorities; the PWA label alone does not prove offline journey operation.

graphs.title: Failure and recovery map
graphs.subtitle: Implemented fallback destinations and open verification areas.
rows: Timing → defaults; language registry → built-in language choices; Piper registry → empty registry.
Shared guided start alerts and stops; Sleep caller catches and stops; Shot catch uses stopShot; Experiment catch returns to experiment.
Mantra soft-fails and restores music; Piper falls back to browser; browser speech error/timeout releases wait.
Media error/rejected play → fade / unavailable → Begin dispatcher; stalled media enters buffer recovery.
Geolocation → approximate sky; wake lock/output selection unsupported → continue.
Some reads have guards; many localStorage writes are direct. Precache addAll has no partial-install fallback.
Cancel pending narration/generation and guide waits; stop playback; return screen.
Slow network, page hidden, mobile audio interruption, rapid double Begin/Restart, cache upgrades and storage denial.
notes: Not every async failure is caught by the top-level window.onerror handler. Missing boundaries are shown as verification work rather than invented successful recovery.
